content.text: {"label":"none","explanation":"The only alert is payments staffing at 22 agents against 27.5 expected (-20%). Our own 16:15 action moved 5 cross-skilled agents from payments to general for 16:30-20:00, and 27.5 - 5 = 22.5, so the gap comes almost entirely from that move. It is not an absence or other supply problem: zero absences are logged on either queue. There are no customer-impacting incidents and no marketing entries. Volume is running above forecast (payments +13-22%, general +15-22% in recent intervals), spread fairly evenly across call reasons. Even so, both queues have held 100% service level with zero abandons in every interval since 16:00, helped by the levers already in place. The day is not currently off target.","plan_name":"Hold current plan, monitor only","rationale":"Service level is 100% on both queues, well above the 80/20 target. The overtime (16:00-20:00), cross-skill move, coaching cancellation, callback and chat deflection already cover the rest of the day. Overtime offered so far is about 43 agents x 2 h x 40% acceptance x Rs 360, roughly Rs 12,400, close to the Rs 15,000 daily budget. More overtime or deflection would add cost with no service benefit. A second break delay on payments would mostly skip agents already delayed today. If payments service level later falls toward 80%, the first free lever is to return some of the 5 cross-skilled agents from general, which also has ample headroom. For now, no new actions are proposed.","actions":[]}
